title: Robots staff shops and theme parks across China during the Golden Week holiday
source_used: 36Kr English (eu.36kr.com; read in full from the pre-fetched text); the piece comes from the WeChat account Yuan Media Hub, written by Xie Chunsheng, published with 36Kr authorization
key_facts: During China's National Day (Golden Week) holiday there were 826 million domestic tourist trips and 738.375 billion yuan of tourism spending, up 6.3% and 4.3% year on year on a daily-average basis.

More than 30 embodied-intelligence and robotics firms have entered tourism, retail and consumer service this year, with thousands of 'on-duty' robots at scenic spots during the holiday (incomplete statistics).

Agibot and Chimelong launched what they call the world's first large-scale embodied-intelligence theme park at Hengqin Chimelong Spaceship Park in Zhuhai, with more than 300 robots in retail, guiding and science education.

Galaxy General's 'Galaxy Space Capsule' robot stores, with the Galbot G1 humanoid taking orders and payments, cover about 50 cities and around 200 locations; Galbot G1 also works in a FamilyMart in Beijing.

Cross-Dimensional Intelligence's 30-plus stations received over 110,000 visitors in the holiday; its flagship earned up to 150,000 yuan; a Zhifang Robotics store exceeded 200,000 yuan in monthly revenue.
Traditional convenience stores are struggling: in the first half of 2026, 50% of sampled stores saw sales fall, per the China Chain Store and Franchise Association.

A listed convenience-store firm suspended a robot vending project after a year because it had not reached the standard for large-scale use; weak points include grabbing errors on real shelves, long task chains such as making coffee, and no mature after-sales repair network.
The article says the real test is whether the robots still look worthwhile once the novelty fades.
quote_evidence: According to incomplete statistics, more than 30 embodied intelligence and robotics enterprises have entered cultural tourism, retail and consumer service scenarios this year, with the number of "on-duty" robots at scenic spots reaching thousands during the National Day holiday.

This A-share listed convenience store enterprise suspended its robot vending system project after one year of deployment, for the simple reason that it has not yet reached the standard for large-scale commercial implementation.
This article is from the WeChat official account "Yuan Media Hub", written by Xie Chunsheng, and published with authorization from 36Kr.
why_it_matters_hint: Chinese robot makers are using holiday crowds at tourist sites as a public test of shop and guide robots.
event_date: National Day holiday (1 to 8 Oct 2026); article 10 Oct 2026
notes: Business-press feature written from company disclosures; revenue and visitor figures are company-supplied and not independently checked. The author's claim that the robot stores are 'not staged' and 'making substantial profits' is not repeated as fact. The 'world's first' theme park label is Agibot's.
